title: enclosed space entry explained: no permit, no entry
description: Enclosed spaces on board can hold an atmosphere that cannot support life, with no warning to the senses. The precautions every seafarer must follow before entry: permit, isolation, ventilation, testing, attendant and rescue readiness.

source.title: Revised recommendations for entering enclosed spaces aboard ships (resolution A.1050(27))

script: An enclosed space can look perfectly safe, and still hold no air that you can breathe. Rust, some cargoes and fresh coatings use up oxygen, and toxic gases collect in tanks and void spaces. Your senses will not warn you. Before anyone enters, test the atmosphere from outside. Oxygen should read 21% by volume, with flammable and toxic gases within your procedure's limits. Get the entry permit. Isolate and ventilate the space. Test the atmosphere, and keep monitoring it. Post an attendant at the entrance with agreed communications. And have rescue equipment ready. If someone collapses inside, do not rush in. Raise the alarm, and enter only as a trained rescue team with breathing apparatus. No permit, no test, no entry. Every time.
